Riley Trettel (Energy & Data Center Development at SpaceX) in yesterdays Cochise Data Center meeting. 

He claims the project will deliver up to:
- 40% off residential power bills for Sulphur Springs members, for the life of the project
- $53 million a year to the SSVEC Foundation, for education and the community
- $190 million a year in extra capital for Sulphur Springs, for projects or back to members
- $200 million a year for AEPCO and its members. About $100 million of that for Sulphur Springs
- $3.6 billion in new power lines, paid by SpaceX and given to the co-op. The co-op takes on no debt
- $30 to $100 million a year in new property tax, and a 20% cut in everyone else's county property taxes
- $250 million, one time, in sales tax. He said it could pay off the jail bond and fund the sheriff, fire districts, and the hospital
- $50 billion invested in the project
- 1,000 permanent jobs and 5,000 construction jobs
- No industrial water. Water for staff and maintenance about equal to 20–30 homes a year
- No gas turbines and no power plant on the site. The computers buy power from the co-op grid
- Dark-sky lighting, pointed at the ground
- Cooling equipment more than 1,500 feet from any neighboring property line or public road

This project is clearly extremely positive for the area.

The irony of all the attacks on @elonmusk over DOGE is that cutting government spending and regulation is the solution to the cost-of-living crisis

And the things getting more expensive the fastest are the most regulated: housing, healthcare, and education 

TVs, software, cellphones, and toys got cheaper

Elon Musk and DOGE would have made life more affordable for Americans if they were allowed to cut spending and get rid of unnecessary regulations

Had coffee with a right-leaning friend who works as a general contractor. He said his daily life was mostly the same between the last two years of the Biden term and the first two years of the Trump term, with one exception: it now costs $230 to fill his truck with diesel.

I actually feel bad for Elon, even though I deeply disagree with him on some things.

Imagine trying to build a car company in California in the mid-2000s, when American manufacturing is being completely offshored and almost all of Wall Street thinks you’re a joke and is rooting for your failure, while the entire oil and gas industry is using all their power and leverage to make you fail. 

But against all odds, you actually pull it off. You build cars that make electric vehicles desirable to millions of people, create an enormous number of quality American jobs, and force the global car industry to play catch up and move away from oil and gas.

You would think California would be proud of you and the team. Instead you find yourself having to fight a completely corrupt and incompetent left government impeding all your efforts while you sleep at the factory night after night to avoid collapse. At some point, you would go to the right too.

And because of your politics, it becomes a justification for people to celebrate your companies failing in their personal ideological fight with you. Even threats against you become something people explain away and use mental gymnastics to justify.

Meanwhile, people like Scott Galloway and Bernie Sanders who have made absolutely nobody better off other than themselves get to lecture you about your value to society and even call for your murder without grounds from their vacation home while you're on 20 hour benders in your factories trying to get things built for all of society. If this were me I would lose my mind.

Criticize his opinions. I do sometimes, especially on Ukraine. But the pleasure people take in wanting to destroy everything he’s built is hideous and frankly suicidal for the masses, especially coming from people who insist they care about workers, the climate, and civilization as a whole. 

As you try to make good things for society you are confronted with a world that worships people who care only about the perception of being good people, while they actually fight against your tangible efforts of making improvements for humanity.

I don't think almost anyone would have made it out of that and if they did, they would probably not come away feeling so warm towards the left either.  So I am rooting for Elon to succeed, and for humanity.

The governor-elect of Texas, Gina Hinojosa, has explicitly said that all currently permitted datacenters in Texas will be allowed to finish construction. This essentially covers all of the 2027 and likely well into 2028.

She is going to pass laws that ensure that all *newly* permitted datacenters going forward for delivery in 2028/2029 will pay taxes, commit to no increase in power prices for consumers, don’t impact water availability for people, be constructed with union labor and give “Texans a seat at the table.”

Sounds reasonable. She doesn’t want to lose a lot of good blue collar jobs and property taxes for small towns in rural Texas.

Photorealistic 15-second vertical smartphone video of Finn, a real black house cat, working as a barista in a busy, authentic neighborhood coffee shop.

Only his head, upper torso, and two front paws are visible above the countertop. His front paws rest naturally ON the counter, ready to operate the equipment. He is NEVER sitting, standing, or walking on top of the counter.

Customer's POV, filmed from directly across the counter at eye level, slightly handheld. A real working cafe with professional espresso machines, stacked cups, shelves, warm lighting, and realistic background activity. Finn wears a plain dark barista apron.

Quick sequence:

Finn stands behind the payment terminal, paws resting on the counter, staring seriously at the customer.

He turns sideways and uses one front paw to press the espresso machine button. Coffee pours into a cup.

He grabs a small plain milk carton with both paws, pours milk into a metal pitcher, and sneaks a quick lick.

He works the steam wand, then carefully pours milk into the espresso, making surprisingly beautiful latte art.

He proudly presents the finished latte to the customer, both paws resting on the counter. The customer takes it. Finn immediately starts grooming one paw, completely unbothered.

Fast, natural editing, realistic feline body movements, subtle humor, convincing physical interactions, and consistent cafe layout.

Finn should feel like a REAL CAT who somehow has a legitimate barista job, not a cat playing with coffee equipment.

No logos, branding, signage, visible text, or watermarks. No cartoon styling, human hands on Finn, or full-body shots of him on the counter.
